title: Best free AI lip sync tools (2026): limits & watermarks
summary: Find a free lip sync workflow for video or a portrait. Compare no-signup trials, duration limits, watermarks, local software, and when paying helps.
body_markdown:
Start with[Magic Hour Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) for a free browser trial using your own face video and audio: three guest attempts per day, up to ten seconds each, with a watermark. For a still portrait, use[Talking Photo](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-talking-photo) instead. Free generation, watermark-free downloading, and commercial permission are three different conditions.

These are different workflows, not four interchangeable video editors. Offers were checked September 9, 2026. Magic Hour publishes this comparison; it is based on documented access and inputs, not a measured quality ranking.


### Lip-sync your own clip


Upload a video and audio track to Magic Hour, generate a short sample, and check timing around consonants and head turns.


[Try Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync)


## 1. Magic Hour: try your own footage without signup


Upload a short video with one clear face and a separate audio recording. A front-facing clip with little camera movement makes a useful first attempt. Include a pause so you can see whether the mouth closes when the speaker stops.


For a simple trial, say: “Hello, Maya. Your preview is ready.” Record it clearly and keep it within the ten-second limit. Use your own footage or media you have permission to edit. Open[Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) , add both files, generate, and inspect the complete video.


Free results carry a watermark. If the sample fits your project, compare the[paid plans](https://magichour.ai/pricing) for longer work, credit usage, watermark-free video, and commercial use. Do not purchase a longer run to fix a face that is already distorted in the short one; change the input first.


## 2. Talking Photo: use a portrait directly


The[Talking Photo tool](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-talking-photo) starts from a still image and audio. Its current FAQ states three guest attempts per day and a five-second free clip limit. Record a short line such as “Welcome back. Let's get started,” rather than squeezing a paragraph into the sample.


Choose a clear portrait with one visible face and space around the chin. Start with a natural expression and unobstructed eyes and mouth. Watch for moving teeth, changing face shape, and a jaw that keeps moving during silence.


A talking photo exports a video. It does not inherit the watermark-free policy of Magic Hour's free still-image tools. For a detailed shortlist, read[best AI talking-photo tools](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-talking-photo-tools-2026) .


## 3. HeyGen: evaluate a presenter workflow


[HeyGen's free plan](https://www.heygen.com/pricing) lists three videos per month, each up to one minute. Premium features have limited trial access. Watermark removal is listed under paid Creator, so do not treat the free allowance as a promise of client-ready exports.


Use this route when your main task is building a presenter video from a script. Before generating the full message, check the available avatar, voice pronunciation, and export settings.


## 4. SadTalker: run a talking-photo model yourself


[SadTalker](https://github.com/OpenTalker/SadTalker) takes an image and audio to create a talking face. The repository states an Apache 2.0 license and documents installation. Local processing has hardware and setup costs even without a subscription; additional dependencies and model files may have separate terms.


Choose it when operating the software is part of your goal. A hosted community demo is a separate service, so its availability and free allowance cannot be inferred from the repository.


## What does “free” include?


Check the finished download, not only the generation button. A useful free trial should answer whether your actual source works before you commit time or money to a larger project.

## Make the first attempt count


1. Choose one visible speaker and trim a short, continuous shot.
2. Record one clear line. Avoid overlapping speakers and loud background music.
3. Match the clip and audio lengths as closely as practical.
4. Generate once and watch the downloaded result with sound.
5. If it fails, change the source or the specific problem before spending the next attempt.


For a walkthrough with upload screenshots, see[how to lip sync a video](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-lip-sync-a-video-with-ai) .


## When a paid plan is worth considering


Upgrade when the sample is already usable and your project needs more duration, more attempts, the paid mode, or a qualifying export. A paid tier is not evidence of better results on every input.


For a client deliverable, approve one representative sample before generating every language or version. Keep the script, face source, and voice permissions with the project. See the[full lip sync comparison](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-lip-sync-tools) for subscription and usage-cost examples.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is there a free lip sync tool with no signup?


Yes. Magic Hour's guest video tool offers three attempts per day without an account, up to ten seconds each. Free video includes a watermark.


### Can I get free lip sync without a watermark?


This guide does not verify a hosted service offering unlimited, watermark-free lip sync at no charge. For Magic Hour, watermark-free video is a paid-plan benefit. Local open-source software is another route if you can operate it and satisfy the relevant licenses.


### Does a free account include unlimited credits?


No. Guest allowances, account offers, and paid credits are separate. Check the balance and limits shown in the current account instead of relying on an older signup-credit figure.


### Why does the output look wrong?


Check the face visibility, audio clarity, and timing first. A side-facing mouth, an obstruction, or overlapping voices can make the task harder. If the whole track is consistently early or late, check the input timing before regenerating.
